non_regression_invariants: The active specialist is read from exactly one selector key and is never inferred from a service name, run-directory version, dashboard label, or saved goal prose.

Training preflight, terminal gate handling, stable operator checks, and transition validation resolve specialist_runtime_registry_v1.json from POKEBOT_SPECIALIST_RUNTIME_ROOT; independently mutable registry copies may not become runtime truth.
Successor selection and prestage read the mutable specialist projection only from /home/inzi/poke-bot-agent/state/specialists.yaml; deployment-directory copies are never selection authority.
The gate-handler CLI bootstraps its runtime import path and must resolve the identical validated command from the managed service and from an arbitrary operator working directory.
The logical required roster is read only from active_expert_ids; V6 physical matchup rows and parameter expectations are derived from fixed slot_capacity and the instantiated per-slot architecture.
The transition graph and its node payloads contain no specialist, deck, checkpoint-version, deployment-version, date-window, or run-name literals.
Specialist-specific assets live in the runtime registry or immutable receipts, not in service files, task-graph nodes, or launcher branches.
An active trainer blocks transition execution. Pre-staging is read-only and may never mutate the selector, runtime registry, model, gate, or service state.

Independent preparation and validation tasks run concurrently by default. Sequential barriers are allowed only for explicit artifact, checksum, immutable-receipt, selector-boundary, memory-guard, or single-active-learner dependencies; healthy production may not be preempted or starved for preparation.
No interactive SSH, Codex, terminal, editor, or user session may be terminated or treated as stale.
Only the active specialist may receive gradients, optimizer steps, replay updates, rehearsal updates, or checkpoint publication.
Completed specialists and original passing checkpoints remain immutable; V5 derivatives are inference-only compatibility artifacts.
Every later specialist hot-starts from the latest checksum-accepted cumulative core, never a fixed historical core.

The expanded strategic-head architecture contains exactly 11 canonical heads and follows the checksum-bound cumulative 25-epoch schedule. Before revision-16 activation runtime_enabled_heads remain empty; afterward all 17 required non-matchup, non-guide heads feed the checksum-bound fused action path.

Completed V5 specialists may gain expanded heads only through separately registered derivative artifacts after the first expanded-head cumulative core is frozen; originals remain immutable and only one explicitly active retrofit learner may update.
Bootstrap remains exactly 25 supervised epochs. Baseline RL remains 8192 new games per iteration with a 7168/1024 split and 5-RL/5-rehearsal cadence.
Research evaluations never enter any training, replay, rehearsal, or update path, and established gate thresholds may not be silently changed.
The active iteration floor and ceiling are 5 and 15 completed iterations for every specialist. Historical bounds remain evidence only.
Kaggle quota or spacing never blocks the next specialist or population transition, and delayed submissions always reference the original frozen checkpoint.
A daily expert refresh never changes an in-progress update; a new receipt activates only at a safe bootstrap or rehearsal boundary.
Bert deletes a downloaded daily archive only after Elmo commits the identical checksum; Inzi never carries the large replay archive.
No dashboard or planning file is allowed to override runtime state.
